name: Norway

findings.summary: Telia Norway named Ericsson sole supplier of its 5G radio network, with Ericsson eventually supplying RAN for all its technologies; rollout from 2020 with nationwide 5G coverage targeted by end-2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so the pole is third. RAN only; Light Reading says Nokia was earlier named Telia's Nordic-Baltic packet-core vendor (not coded separately). Value undisclosed. Whether the full swap finished by 2023 was not confirmed in this pass, so still_current is null.

findings.reversal_of: Huawei 4G radio access network at Telia Norway
findings.summary: Telia Norway dropped Huawei, its 4G radio supplier, from its 5G network and RAN plans; Ericsson was to replace Huawei radio equipment, with the swap expected complete by 2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a reversal of an operational (tier 5) Huawei 4G RAN. Telia gave no public reason; telecoms.com only speculates about parent-company ties to Ericsson, so the reason is coded commercial. Completion of the swap not confirmed in this pass.

findings.summary: Telenor chose Ericsson as its main 5G radio-network supplier in Norway; Nokia and Ericsson were already its 5G core vendors, with Huawei given no core role.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Swedish) and Nokia (Finnish) are both third-pole vendors. Telenor is Norway's largest operator, so scale is national. Value undisclosed.

findings.reversal_of: Huawei 4G radio access network at Telenor Norge (majority phase-out)
findings.summary: Telenor began phasing out Huawei, its 4G partner of about a decade, replacing most Huawei radio gear over four to five years, while Huawei kept a limited role upgrading and maintaining parts of the network.
findings.analyst_inference: Partial reversal of an operational (tier 5) Huawei 4G RAN. Telenor's CEO cited a holistic evaluation covering security, technical quality, commercial terms and innovation, not politics; coded commercial, though the security element makes geopolitical arguable. A 4-5 year phase-out implies completion around 2023-24; not confirmed, and Huawei's residual role is unquantified.

findings.summary: Nscale and Aker formed a 50/50 joint venture to build Stargate Norway at Kvandal near Narvik: 230MW planned plus 290MW ambition, about US$1bn for the first phase, OpenAI as initial offtaker.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole left null because the owner-operator is an equal JV of a Norwegian firm (Aker, domestic) and a UK firm (Nscale, third); control is genuinely shared. Tier 3 rests on the JV agreement plus the binding Microsoft offtake (NOR-006); construction start and JV closing were not confirmed. Announced value is the initial-phase figure.

findings.summary: The Aker-Nscale joint venture signed a five-year binding agreement worth about US$6.2bn to provide Microsoft with GPU infrastructure at Narvik, with staged deployments from 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Microsoft is the tenant, not the controller; the facility pole follows the shared Aker/Nscale owner-operator (null, see NOR-005). Only the company release was opened (S1), so confidence medium. Whether deployments have begun in 2026 was not confirmed.

findings.summary: Stargate Norway targets 100,000 Nvidia GPUs at the Narvik site by the end of 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 1 because the GPU count is a stated target; no Nvidia purchase order, delivery or export documentation was found. The Microsoft release (NOR-006) does not name the GPU model.

findings.local_actor: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
findings.summary: NTNU's NorwAI released Norwegian-language models, including from-scratch NorGPT models (2023) and continually pretrained Mistral, Mixtral, Llama2 and Magistral variants (2024-25), trained on NTNU's own cluster and offered for Nordic research use.
findings.analyst_inference: Weights held by a Norwegian public university, so domestic. Base model recorded as the latest Magistral-24B (Mistral AI, French, third); the family also includes Llama2 (US) and from-scratch models. Coded tier 2 as a research release, not national government adoption. The National Library's Mimir project (17 models, 2024) is related but not separately coded.

applications.null_reason: one search found a January 2023 Storting written answer leaving Chinese camera risk to individual agencies; no ban, removal order or named safe-city/e-gov AI deployment found

power.null_reason: no dedicated AI/DC power plant surfaced; Narvik site described as grid-connected renewable supply

research_gaps: Did Telia Norway and Telenor Norge complete their Huawei RAN swap-outs (targets 2023 and ~2023-24), and does Huawei retain any maintenance or coverage role at Telenor?
Has Norway adopted any formal vendor-screening rule for telecoms (follow-up to Meld. St. 9 (2022-2023) or the new ekom law) that restricts Huawei/ZTE? Search found only 2019 deliberations and no ban.
Stargate Norway: has the Aker-Nscale JV closed, has construction started at Kvandal, and have Nvidia GPUs (model, count) been delivered for the Microsoft contract in 2026?
Ice (Lyse) network vendors: the third mobile operator's RAN and core suppliers were not searched.
Other large Norwegian data-centre projects since 2023 (Green Mountain, Bulk, Stack, Lefdal) and their controllers were not searched.
Has the Norwegian government entered a partnership with OpenAI under 'OpenAI for Countries' beyond the Stargate offtake, or with any other frontier provider?
Do Norwegian public bodies still operate Hikvision/Dahua cameras, and has any agency removed them after NSM warnings?
